clue.text: Mrs Blair wraps a tender rump steak in shop

indicators.note: to wrap is to enclose, so the first name goes around everything that follows it
a rump is the hind end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: Cherie Blair, wife of former Prime Minister Tony Blair
taken as written
the tail end of the word tender
a steak is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: The former PM's wife wraps a juicy piece of rump steak in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender rump steak' reads as one cut of meat, but 'rump' belongs to 'tender' (its last letter) and 'steak' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A charcuterie is a delicatessen specialising in cooked and cured pork products, a kind of shop.

clue.text: Cute rear wobbles in wild thing

indicators.note: something that wobbles is unsteady and out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A wild animal's pretty backside wobbles as it moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living animal, and a wild thing is one living outside human care.

clue.text: Blakey, say, is to strive for mastery

blocks.note: Art Blakey was an American jazz drummer; 'say' marks him as an example of the name
taken as written
to try is to strive

explanation.surface: A musician striving to perfect his craft.
explanation.walkthrough: Blakey suggests the pop artist Peter Blake, nudging toward ARTIST, but the name is the jazz drummer's first name, Art.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or mastery of an art form, a close synonym.

clue.text: Scoundrel one above a papal court

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible man
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rogue placed above others in the Pope's court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above' just orders the pieces in a down entry: one sits on top of the a.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the administrative body of the Holy See, the Pope's court in Rome.

clue.text: Romanov apologist in Dire Straits…

indicators.note: being in a dire state means being in a mess, so the following word is disordered

blocks.note: the fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: A defender of the Russian royal family finds himself in a desperate plight, or perhaps the rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits looks like the name of the band, but it splits into an anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist supports rule by the tsar, and the Romanovs were the last Russian tsarist dynasty.

clue.text: …slippery sort in band having a dance

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another, so the sort sits within the band

blocks.note: a ring is a band, as round a finger
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A slippery character in a musical group takes to the floor, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to perform a reel, a lively Scottish folk dance, so reeling is dancing one.

clue.text: Neat prose lost in language

indicators.note: words that are lost have gone astray, so their letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Tidy writing gets lost in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international language invented in the 1880s.

clue.text: Violin player Clara or Dicky?

blocks.note: first meaning: the rod drawn across the strings is what plays a violin
second meaning: Clara ___ was a silent-film star

explanation.walkthrough: 'Violin player' suggests a musician, but it is the implement; 'Clara or Dicky' asks for the word completing both names.
explanation.definitionFit: The stick with horsehair sounds a violin, and the same word follows Clara (the actress) and dicky (a bow tie).

clue.text: Revealing report about first king?

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a report is a loud bang, as of a gun
read cryptically: R (king, from Rex) then I (first, one)

explanation.surface: A revealing account of the earliest monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First king' looks like a single idea, but it is read in reverse order as king (R) followed by first (I).
explanation.definitionFit: Baring something means uncovering it, exposing it to view.

clue.text: See 18
Conservative leaving America's heart to submit

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: the American spelling of centre, a heart
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician leaves the US mainland to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's' signals the US spelling CENTER rather than British CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something, such as a plea or an entry form, is to submit it formally.

clue.text: Had MP spoken without consideration for time?

blocks.note: to have a meal is to eat it, so had = ate
taken as written
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Did a Member of Parliament talk without regard to the clock?
explanation.definitionFit: Atemporal means independent of or unaffected by time, outside time altogether.

clue.text: Maestro to study in India

blocks.note: taken as written
to scan is to study closely
taken as written
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A conductor goes off to train in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the study somewhere, but it is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, and conductors are addressed as maestro.

clue.text: Letter on doormat contains music

indicators.note: the phrase holds the word within it, spread across the boundary between two words

blocks.note: the end of letter, all of on, the start of doormat

explanation.surface: A letter lying on the doormat turns out to contain sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme returns between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Dish of baked brie rodent devours

indicators.note: baking transforms something, so the cheese's letters are cooked into a new arrangement
to devour is to swallow whole, so the animal takes the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a rat is a rodent
the fodder

explanation.surface: A rat gobbles up a plate of baked cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is a dish of melted cheese sauce on toast.

clue.text: Criminal around Yale: he's silly

definitions.note: a noun here, as in 'you silly'

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the criminal encloses the rest

blocks.note: criminal behaviour is bad
Yale is a well-known brand of lock
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook hanging round a university who is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale looks like the university, but it is the lock maker; 'silly' is used as a noun meaning a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead is a stupid person, and 'a silly' is informal for the same.

clue.text: Wilder say catlike mammal losing tail

indicators.note: an animal losing its tail is cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a genet is a small spotted catlike carnivore

explanation.surface: A wilder kind of cat has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' reads as an adjective describing the animal; it is the comic actor Gene Wilder, with 'say' marking him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Wilder was the American actor of Willy Wonka fame, so Wilder is an example of someone called Gene.

clue.text: Strategic first act in short talk

indicators.note: placed inside, so the opening act sits within the shortened word

blocks.note: the outer letters as the setter must intend them; no reading of short talk yields these letters cleanly
Act I, the first act of a play

explanation.surface: A shrewd opening move in a brief speech.
explanation.walkthrough: ACT I in TAL (talk cut short) gives TACTIAL, one C short; the blogger at Fifteensquared could not account for the extra C either.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical and strategic both describe planning to gain an advantage, near synonyms in everyday use.

clue.text: Find fault with badly dressed dish

blocks.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
dowdy means unfashionably dressed

explanation.surface: Criticising a shabbily presented plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' looks like an anagram signal, but 'badly dressed' is simply a definition of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandowdy is an American baked fruit dessert topped with pastry, a dish.

clue.text: Fish small — batter rubbish

blocks.note: a cod is a fish
S is the abbreviation for small
to batter is to wallop, hit hard

explanation.surface: A small fish in batter, as at a British chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' suggests fried fish coating, but it is the verb meaning to hit. Codswallop is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is a colloquial word for nonsense, and rubbish is used in the same sense.

clue.text: Winger Mike appears in Italian league

indicators.note: appearing in something means being found within it, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: Serie A is Italy's top football division
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A wide player called Mike turns out in Italian football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' reads as a footballer, but it means anything with wings, here a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The seriema is a long-legged South American bird, and a winger is something that flies.

clue.text: Moon featuring in play's miniature scene

indicators.note: to feature in something is to be part of it, so the moon goes inside the play

blocks.note: a play is a drama
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: The moon appears as a prop in a theatre production's tiny set.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model representing a scene, often in miniature.

clue.text: Student inside called up courtesan

indicators.note: one thing set inside another, so the student goes within the word for called
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: to hail someone is to call to them
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student who is called in to see a lady of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah, who betrayed Samson in the Bible, is a byword for a seductive, treacherous woman.

clue.text: On which adders slide to and fro?

definitions.text: On which adders slide to and fro?

blocks.clueFragment: On which adders slide to and fro?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place where snakes slither back and forth
setter's reading: adders are people who add up, and the beads on this counting frame slide along wires

explanation.walkthrough: Adders look like snakes, but they are people doing sums.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame whose beads are pushed back and forth along rods for arithmetic.

clue.text: Bar attracting certain elements

blocks.note: surface reading: a pub that draws in a particular crowd
setter's reading: a metal bar that pulls in iron, nickel and cobalt, the chemical elements it acts on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements' suggests a section of society; it means chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet is a common shape of permanent magnet, attracting ferromagnetic metals such as iron.

clue.text: Pound lender invests in space

indicators.note: to invest can mean to clothe or surround, so the lender wraps around the pound

blocks.note: a bank lends money
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A financier puts money into a space venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invests' reads as finance alongside lender and pound, but here it means to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank is an empty space, as on a form left to be filled in.

clue.text: Demoted Cardinal entertains envoy

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside, so the colour holds the other word

blocks.note: cardinal is a deep red colour
a legate is a papal envoy

explanation.surface: A churchman stripped of rank still plays host to a papal emissary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests the churchman, but it is the colour red.
explanation.definitionFit: To be relegated is to be moved to a lower rank or division, demoted.

clue.text: Poor mark from school master

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A low grade handed out by a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School master' reads as one teacher, but splits into two pieces; gamma is the third Greek letter, used as a low grade in British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: In British academic marking, grades run alpha, beta, gamma, so a gamma is a poor result.

clue.text: Fish gone bad in lobster trap

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoiled, so its letters are jumbled
placed inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the trap

blocks.note: a creel is a wicker basket used to trap lobsters
the fodder

explanation.surface: A fish that has gone off is found in a lobster pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone bad' reads as a description of the fish, but 'bad' is the anagram signal for 'gone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger eel is a large marine eel, a fish found in European waters.

clue.text: Mother Watts circling about parrot

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so the outer letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
W is the symbol for watts
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Mrs Watts circles around a pet parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother Watts' looks like a person's name, but splits into two pieces that together surround the third.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America.

clue.text: Good person retaining current position

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so the good person holds the other letter within

blocks.note: St, abbreviation for saint
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A decent person hangs on to the job they have now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current position' reads as someone's present job, but 'current' is the electrical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit is to position oneself, or of a thing to be placed somewhere, a verb sense of position.

clue.text: End depression in US desert reserve

blocks.note: death is the end of life
a valley is a depression in the land

explanation.surface: Someone ends their gloom in an American desert park.
explanation.definitionFit: Death Valley in California is a desert protected as a US national park, hence reserve.
